papers.title: PIT and Reconstruction for Sums of Powers
papers.abstract: We study deterministic black-box polynomial identity testing (PIT) and reconstruction for polynomials of the form \[ f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^r \alpha_i f_i(x)^d, \] where each $f_i$ belongs to some underlying polynomial class $\mathcal{C}$. This representation generalizes Waring decomposition, several natural small-depth circuit models, and polynomial decompositions arising in moment-based learning problems. Our main results are three lifting theorems showing that, when the outer power is sufficiently large, PIT and reconstruction for the inner class can be lifted to sums of powers. When the power degree is small, we can perform these tasks directly in some of the cases using closure properties of the underlying models. In particular we obtain the following results: \begin{itemize} \item When the inner polynomials have bounded-individual-degrees and are sparse, we obtain deterministic reconstruction for every d: the original power-sum decomposition is recovered at high degree, while at low degree the polynomial is reconstructed nonproperly by sparse interpolation. \item For sums of powers of same-order and any-order read-once oblivious algebraic branching programs, the same proper/nonproper dichotomy gives deterministic reconstruction for every powering degree. \item Explicit quasipolynomial-size hitting sets for every powering degree for several depth-5 and depth-6 circuit families, as well for the models mentioned above. Our results for high powering degree rely on the polynomial ABC theorem, which to the best of our knowledge is the first application of this theorem in the context of PIT.

papers.title: Quadratic Extractors
papers.abstract: A quadratic source is a random variable $X\sim\mathbb{F}_2^n$ generated by applying $n$ quadratics to a hidden uniform string. Previously, the best-known explicit extractor for this model required min-entropy roughly $k=n-\sqrt{\log n}$. In this paper, we give an explicit construction for min-entropy $k=\mathrm{polylog}(n)$. Even for the special case of $2$-local sources, where each bit of $X$ depends on two hidden uniform bits, achieving an entropy requirement below $k=\sqrt{n}$ was an important open problem. This is because such sources provably cannot be reduced (in a black-box manner) to our most powerful general-purpose seedless extractor, known as a sumset extractor. Our new extractor bypasses this barrier, providing the first explicit construction to go beyond sumset extraction.

papers.title: Degree profiles of uniform polynomial consequences: Linear lower bounds for Nullstellensatz and Polynomial Calculus
papers.abstract: This paper proves asymptotically optimal linear degree lower bounds for Nullstellensatz and Polynomial Calculus, yielding a four-way polynomial-versus-exponential proof-size classification for uniform polynomial consequences over fields of positive characteristic. The size bounds use full, explicit coefficient lists, including zeros. Apart from a fixed finite initial range, exactly one of four cases occurs: $\mathrm T_1$, bounded degree; $\mathrm T_2$, degree at least linear in the universe size $n$; $\mathrm T_3$, constant degree on some residue classes and at least linear degree on the others; or $\mathrm T_4$, infinitely many recurring finite degrees, with bounded-degree subsequences and finite $\Omega(n)$ peaks at arbitrarily large sizes. Thus the size patterns are polynomial bounds, exponential lower bounds, a periodic mixture, or polynomial subsequences with finite exponential peaks, respectively. Underivable targets have degree $\infty$, and both proof systems assign the same type. The result strengthens my 2008--2009 refutation classification and extends it to uniform consequences. The proof uses degree-preserving lifting with onset and period bounds linear in the degree. A common $p$-adic hardness spectrum describes the four types topologically. Distinguishing any two types is undecidable already for refutations. The linear degree bounds, four-way classification and pairwise undecidability results have been formalised and verified in Lean. The Lean formalisation, verification records and an accompanying tutorial are available in the supporting materials (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23965838).

papers.title: A New Characterization of Streaming Decidability of Boolean CSPs Under Deletions
papers.abstract: We characterize the single-pass streaming space complexity of Boolean CSP satisfiability in the strict-turnstile model for every fixed constraint language $\Gamma$ of $k$-ary Boolean relations that is not trivially satisfiable. Constraints can be inserted or deleted with nonnegative multiplicities; satisfiability is decided for those remaining at the end. While Sharma and Velusamy [ESA 2026] characterized insertion-only complexity via non-redundancy (up to logarithmic factors), we show that strict-turnstile complexity is governed by the integer capturing degree. For $R\subseteq\{0,1\}^k$, let $d_R$ be the minimum degree of an integer-coefficient polynomial vanishing exactly on $R$ over the Boolean hypercube, and set $d_\Gamma=\max_{R\in\Gamma}d_R$. On polynomial-length streams, we obtain an $O_k(n^{d_\Gamma}\operatorname{polylog} n)$-space randomized algorithm and an $\Omega_k(n^{d_\Gamma}/\log n)$ lower bound for all algorithms. Moreover, our algorithm outputs a sparse instance preserving every satisfying assignment. This yields, to our knowledge, the first insertion-only versus turnstile separation for streaming CSPs. It also differs from the Fourier-degree characterization of exact optimization by Kol, Paramonov, Saxena, and Yu [ITCS 2023]. For $k\ge3$, $k$-XOR with literals has three distinct space complexities: $\widetilde\Theta(n)$ for insertion-only satisfiability, $\widetilde\Theta(n^{\lceil k/2\rceil})$ for strict-turnstile satisfiability, and $\widetilde\Theta(n^k)$ for exact optimization in either model.

papers.title: Asymptotic advantage of quantum one-way and SMP communication for total functions
papers.abstract: We exhibit a total Boolean function on n input bits whose bounded-error quantum simultaneous-message (and hence one-way) communication complexity is in O(\sqrt n), whereas its randomised one-way (and hence simultaneous-message) communication complexity is in \Omega(n). The same function admits a classical simultaneous-message protocol of cost O(\sqrt n) when the players share O(\sqrt n) EPR pairs.

papers.title: Multiplicative and Additive Extractors for Low Entropy Samplable Sources Under Reduced Assumptions
papers.abstract: Trevisan and Vadhan [TV, FOCS'00] constructed (seedless) extractors for distributions samplable by poly-size circuits that have very high min-entropy, under the very strong complexity theoretic hardness assumption that $\mathsf{E}=\mathsf{DTIME}(2^{O(n)})$ requires size $2^{\Omega(n)}$ circuits that have oracle access to $\Sigma_6^{\text{P}}$. In this paper we give three new explicit constructions of extractors for samplable distributions. First, we construct an extractor that extracts one bit, with constant error, for min-entropy $k=O(\log n)$, which matches the non-constructive probabilistic argument. This result uses hardness for nondeterministic circuits, and achieves the same parameters as the recent extractor of Oh and Shaltiel [OS, STOC'26] under an incomparable hardness assumption. In contrast to the extractor of [OS26], our extractor (and, similarly, the constructions below) also works for the more general class of distributions samplable with postselection (a model introduced by [BGDM, FOCS'23] that generalizes samplable and recognizable sources). Second, we construct an extractor that extracts almost all the entropy, with polynomially small error, for min-entropy $k=n^{\alpha}$, where $\alpha>0$ is an arbitrary constant. This result also uses hardness for nondeterministic circuits, and significantly improves upon the recent extractor of [Shaltiel, FOCS'25] which required a much stronger assumption. This extractor is also \textit{multiplicative}: a stronger notion suggested in [AASY, Comp. Complexity'16; Shaltiel, CCC'25] to make extractors for samplable distributions suitable for selecting keys for cryptographic protocols. Third, we construct an extractor that extracts almost all the entropy, with polynomially small error, for min-entropy $k=\mathrm{polylog}(n)$. This result uses hardness for circuits that have oracle access to $\Sigma_2^{\text{P}}$.

papers.title: A Little Derandomization Goes a Long Way: Unconditional Circuit Lower Bounds using Low-Degree PIT
The Proof Analysis Problem for Constant-Depth Frege
papers.abstract: We give a parallel algorithm for the Proof Analysis Problem of Arteche, Atserias, de Rezende, and Khaniki (FOCS 2025). The problem asks, given a CNF formula $\varphi$ on $n$ variables and a proof $\pi$ of a size-$s$ Resolution lower bound on $\varphi$, encoded as $\neg \mathrm{Ref}_s(\varphi)$, to extract a satisfying assignment for $\varphi$ when one exists. The original work gave a polynomial-time extraction algorithm for Resolution refutations that enabled a formalization of the Atserias-M\"uller lower bound (FOCS 2019) in Extended Frege, but it appeared inherently sequential. We devise a new algorithm that performs assignment extraction in low-depth circuit classes. Specifically, we give an assignment extraction algorithm computable by polynomial-size $\mathbf{TC}^0$ circuits and by quasipolynomial-size $\mathbf{AC}^0$ circuits, and we prove the correctness of the latter within quasipolynomial-size $\mathbf{AC}^0$-Frege. This is thanks to a new formalization of the Atserias-M\"uller lower bound in the relativized theory $\mathsf{T}^4_2(\alpha)$ of bounded arithmetic, which corresponds to depth-$4$ Frege systems. This yields quasipolynomial-size $\mathbf{AC}^0$-Frege proofs for a broad class of Resolution lower bounds, making progress on a question of Pudl\'ak. A key feature of our approach is an improved parameter regime where we get $\mathbf{AC}^0$-Frege formalizations of Resolution lower bounds $\neg \mathrm{Ref}_s(\varphi)$ for all $s$, including $s = n^{O(1)}$. W also show that the Proof Analysis Problem for $\mathbf{AC}^0$-Frege is $\mathbf{NP}$-hard under quasipolynomial-time reductions, which rules out certain Atserias-M\"uller-type approaches to the hardness of automating constant-depth Frege. Furthermore, automating $\mathbf{AC}^0$-Frege on Resolution lower bound formulas suffices to automate it on all formulas.

papers.title: Structured Quantum Hardness from Unstructured Assumptions
papers.abstract: Whether useful structured hardness can arise from unstructured assumptions is a fundamental question in complexity and cryptography. The longstanding Bennett-Gill question asks whether $\mathsf{NP}\cap\mathsf{coNP}$ remains hard relative to a random oracle; [GIKKLS, STOC 2023] recently gave a conditional affirmative answer in the classical setting. We establish the quantum analogue: if $\mathsf{UP}\not\subseteq\mathsf{BQP}$, then $\mathsf{NP}^{O}\cap\mathsf{coNP}^{O}\not\subseteq\mathsf{BQP}^{O}$ with probability $1$ over a random oracle $O$. Beyond extending the classical result, this separation has a distinctly quantum significance: Shor's algorithms defeat canonical number-theoretic hardness candidates, while lattice assumptions and other leading post-quantum cryptographic assumptions do not directly supply hard languages with two-sided classical certification on every input. Our conditional oracle separation provides evidence that such structured quantum hardness can nevertheless arise from unstructured sources. Complementing this result, we rule out fully black-box quantum reductions of worst-case quantum hardness in $\mathsf{NP}\cap\mathsf{coNP}$ to post-quantum injective one-way functions and indistinguishability obfuscation. This barrier excludes a broad class of black-box approaches to deriving structured quantum hardness from generic cryptographic primitives, providing partial evidence that the non-black-box techniques in our first result are essential.

papers.title: Combinatorial limitations of list-decoding Reed-Solomon codes
papers.abstract: For infinitely many rates $R \in (0,1)$, we show that full-length Reed-Solomon codes over fields of low characteristic can contain super-polynomially many codewords in a Hamming ball of radius just exceeding the Johnson radius. Over prime fields, we exhibit full-length Reed-Solomon codes of constant rate $R$ with polynomially many codewords in a Hamming ball of relative radius bounded strictly below $1-R$. This refutes a recent conjecture that, over prime fields, list sizes below capacity are always bounded by a constant. Together, these results demonstrate that certain restrictions in recent works on explicit Reed-Solomon codes achieving list-decoding capacity, related to the choice of field or evaluation points or to the list-size guarantee, are inherent.

papers.title: A Universal Threshold Theory for Local Properties of Random Linear Codes
papers.abstract: Thresholds for local properties tell us which guarantees to expect from random linear codes (RLCs) and help us carry those guarantees over to structured codes. A monotone property is $b$-local if a collection of at most $b$ codewords can witness its satisfaction or failure, as in list decoding and list recovery. The threshold of $\mathcal P$ is the code dimension at which the probability that an RLC in $\mathbb{F}_q^n$ satisfies $\mathcal P$ crosses $1/2$ in a sharp transition. We show that the threshold of a $b$-local property $\mathcal P$ is within $O(b)$ dimensions of the expectation threshold. This is the dimension predicted by the best union bound over covers of $\mathcal P$: families of subspaces such that the span of every witness contains at least one member. This gives a general derandomization statement: Any decreasing local property satisfied by RLCs at a given rate holds at a similar rate for pseudorandom ensembles that fool the cover union bound. In addition to previously studied ensembles, these include codes whose parity-check matrix is sampled from a small-bias distribution. Because our threshold characterization applies to all local properties, this derandomization also reaches properties beyond the scope of earlier reductions, including maximum loads in linear hashing for arbitrary input sets, rank-metric list decoding, and list decoding from insertion-deletion errors and burst errors. Our theorem unifies and strengthens prior works on row-symmetric and coordinate-wise linear characterizations, which located the threshold to within $O(q^{2b}\log_q n)$ and $O(b^2+nb/\log_2 q)$ dimensions, respectively. We obtain $O(b)$ error for every $b$-local property, independently of alphabet size. Under suitable pseudorandomness bounds, the rate loss vanishes for every $b=o(n)$, compared to $b=O(\log n)$ for earlier frameworks.

papers.title: Randomized Parallel Complexity of Weakly Convex Optimization
papers.abstract: We study the minimum number of query rounds needed to find approximate stationary points of nonsmooth weakly convex functions, measured by the gradient of the Moreau envelope. Each round permits multiple simultaneous queries. In the stated parameter regime, the standard subgradient rate is optimal in sufficiently high dimensions, even for randomized algorithms making polynomially many parallel queries per round. We then show how the order structure of the real line enables faster search: a deterministic algorithm using only function values achieves logarithmic round complexity, with a further reduction through parallel queries. Matching lower bounds hold even when each query returns the entire subdifferential. Together, these results clarify the role of dimension in determining the benefits of parallel queries for weakly convex optimization.

papers.title: On computing the determinant over a ring
papers.abstract: An algorithm is presented for computing the determinant and the characteristic polynomial of a matrix $A$ over an arbitrary commutative ring R. The algorithm uses $O(n^\omega)$ ring additions, subtractions and multiplications, where $\omega>2$ is a feasible exponent for matrix multiplication, that is, such that two $n\times n$ matrices over R can be multiplied using $O(n^{\omega})$ ring operations. The algorithm involves no division and no zero test, and its control depends only on $n$: for each $n$ it is a straight-line program. The approach combines a polynomial matrix point of view and a block Krylov point of view on the characteristic polynomial, which makes Strassen's elimination of divisions efficient. A bivariate matrix $\lambda I-L(t)$, obtained from $A$ by a homotopy, is compressed in $\log n$ steps, each of which halves the dimension while only doubling the degree in $\lambda$. The cost of the homotopy is controlled by truncating the power series in $t$ at an order that only grows with the compression steps, from a constant to $n$.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage with Sign-Free Proofs: An Oracle Separation between $\mathsf{StoqMA}$ and $\mathsf{MA}$
papers.abstract: Several landmark oracle results (FOCS 2000, FOCS 2025, STOC 2026) establish strict separations along the chain $\mathsf{MA} \subseteq \mathsf{QCMA} \subseteq \mathsf{QMA}$, showing that quantum verification and quantum witnesses can each provide additional power over classical proof systems. These separations, however, use substantial coherent quantum computation, often through the quantum Fourier transform. We prove that a minimal quantum resource already suffices to outperform every classical verifier. Namely, we show the separation $$\mathsf{MA} \subsetneq \mathsf{StoqMA}$$ relative to a classical oracle. The class $\mathsf{StoqMA}$, introduced by Bravyi, Bessen, and Terhal (arXiv 2006), restricts the verifier to classical reversible computation, followed by a single Hadamard-basis measurement. Its power is closely tied to the complexity of stoquastic Hamiltonians, a sign-problem-free and seemingly more tractable class of quantum Hamiltonians. Our separating problem is to determine whether a sparse high-girth graph, given via an adjacency-list oracle, has a large or small Perron--Frobenius eigenvalue. This amounts to a ground-energy estimation task for a related stoquastic Hamiltonian. Our construction builds on a line of work on graph exploration problems with exponential quantum speedups, from welded trees (STOC 2003) to recent constructions (STOC 2021, arXiv 2026).

papers.title: Polynomial-time classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss
papers.abstract: Sampling experiments are a leading approach to demonstrating quantum computational advantage, yet their robustness to experimental noise is not completely understood. We develop a common framework for classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss, including pure loss. For Fock-state boson sampling, Gaussian boson sampling with fixed uniform squeezing, and fermion sampling with magic inputs, we obtain polynomial-time sampling at inverse-polynomial total variation error, for any fixed nonzero overall loss rate, and with high probability over Haar-random interferometers. A milder flatness assumption on the ideal output distribution suffices for quasipolynomial-time simulation without Haar randomness. With constant thermal loss per layer, the same flatness assumption gives polynomial-time simulation at logarithmic depth. Our bounds for Fock-state boson sampling cover both dilute and saturated regimes and become stronger near full input filling: when only a bounded number of input modes are empty, the noisy output for Haar-random interferometers converges, as the number of modes grows, to a distribution independent of the interferometer.
